system.name: Kiwi Design System
system.purpose: A Storybook workspace that separates repository authoring rules from product-facing Kiwi design contracts.
system.framework: React 19 with shadcn/ui (Base UI) and Tailwind CSS 4; legacy surfaces are migrating off Material UI 7
system.sourceOfTruth: This catalog is the canonical source for contract lists. MDX pages and story docs import and render these entries; do not hand-edit a duplicated copy in MDX or stories.

sourceFields.docSource: The MDX file that renders the readable chapter.
sourceFields.storySource: The stories file that provides executable examples and docs.
sourceFields.componentSource: The implementation file that remains the final behavior.

storybookGuide.label: Storybook Guide
owns: Storybook build, accessibility checks, and publishing
doesNotOwn: Kiwi product patterns and domain semantics

kiwi-ui.label: React inside Kiwi UI
kiwi-ui.contract: Use shadcn components from src/components/ui and Tailwind semantic tokens (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, ...). Legacy MUI surfaces keep semantic values from src/Theme.ts until they migrate.
kiwi-ui.avoid: Do not repeat raw color values in product components, mix MUI and Tailwind styling inside one surface, or use the external-app token contract.

external-kiwi-app.label: External Kiwi App
external-kiwi-app.avoid: Do not import internal Kiwi UI theme modules.

reusable-interface-work.label: Reusable interface element
reusable-interface-work.contract: Start with the closest documented component or pattern in this catalog.
reusable-interface-work.avoid: Do not create a local primitive before checking this catalog.

do-avoid.purpose: Present directly comparable recommended and discouraged guidance in Storybook documentation.
useWhen: Readers need to compare two concrete choices or authoring decisions.
Both sides can be expressed as short, independently scannable items.
avoidWhen: The content is a warning, error, or changing system status that needs alert semantics.
The guidance requires a sequence, decision tree, or more than two categories.
accessibility: Use visible Do and Avoid labels in addition to semantic colors.
Choose a heading level that preserves the surrounding document hierarchy.
Provide a concise aria label for the paired guidance region.
do-avoid.responsive: Two columns when the component container can fit two 280px panels; otherwise stacked, independent of the iframe viewport.

colors.summary: Product color comes exclusively from the Tailwind semantic tokens defined in `src/index.css`.
rules: Build product UI with the Tailwind semantic token utilities (`bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`, `text-destructive`, ...); never hard-code color in product components — no raw hex/rgb values and no Tailwind palette classes such as `amber-500`.
`src/index.css` is the single source of truth: token values live on `:root` and reach utilities through the `@theme inline` block.
To add or change a color role, define the custom property in `src/index.css` and expose it in `@theme inline`; do not create component-local palettes or one-off values.

Pick the role that matches meaning: `primary` for main actions, `secondary` for supporting filled actions, `muted`/`accent` for subdued and hover fills, `destructive` for errors and destructive actions, `success` for positive confirmation, `warning` for caution states, `border`/`input`/`ring` for chrome and focus, `chart-1`…`chart-5` for chart series.

Do not add a new token when an existing role already expresses the meaning; surface-specific token sets (a sidebar palette, a per-feature palette) are not allowed unless the surface genuinely diverges from the shared roles.
There is no dark palette yet: `dark:` variants stay inert until a `.dark` token set is defined in `src/index.css`.

typography.summary: Uses Montserrat for ordinary UI, composed as a small set of shadcn/Tailwind type roles.
typography.fontFamily: Montserrat through the `--font-sans` token (aliased by `--font-heading`), self-hosted from @fontsource-variable/montserrat via src/fonts/montserrat.css; `sans-serif` is only a generic fallback for glyphs Montserrat does not cover (e.g. CJK).

roles.label: Page title
roles.use: The single h1 of a page. Rendered by AdminPageHeader; do not restyle it locally.

roles.label: Dialog title
roles.use: The heading of a dialog. Rendered by DialogTitle; do not restyle it locally.

roles.label: Label / emphasized UI text
roles.use: Form labels, table headers, buttons, and other short emphasized UI text.

roles.label: Body UI text
roles.use: Default text on shadcn surfaces: table cells, dialog content, list items, and form values.

roles.label: Supporting text
roles.use: Descriptions, helper text, and secondary copy that accompanies body text.

roles.label: Metadata
roles.use: Timestamps, counts, keyboard hints, and other short annotations. This is the minimum text size; never use it for paragraphs.

rules: Montserrat is the only typeface for ordinary UI; never reintroduce Roboto, Arial, Helvetica, or a platform default stack.
The only exceptions are math (KaTeX/MathJax), monospace for code, commands, IDs, and JSON, the Ace editor, icon fonts, and third-party component internals.
Compose text from the documented type roles before inventing a new size, weight, or tracking combination. For small anchored overlays, use the documented Small Popup typography roles.
When a component owns a role (AdminPageHeader for the page title, DialogTitle for dialog titles, Label for form labels), use the component instead of re-creating its classes.
`text-sm` is the default UI text size on shadcn surfaces; `text-xs` is the minimum and is reserved for short labels and metadata.

The full Tailwind size scale (`text-xs` through `text-9xl`) stays available, but ordinary product UI uses the documented roles; sizes above `text-2xl` are reserved for hero, marketing, or empty-state display text.
Keep heading levels meaningful; visual size and document hierarchy are separate concerns.
Use semantic text color utilities (`text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground`, `text-primary`, `text-destructive`) instead of hard-coded grays.
Surfaces still on MUI keep the semantic variants from `src/Theme.ts` until they migrate; do not mix MUI typography and Tailwind text utilities inside one surface.

useWhen: The user can initiate a discrete action such as create, save, refresh, upload, or delete.
The result and disabled or processing state can be explained with a concise action label.
avoidWhen: The destination is navigation; use a link instead.
The action changes a persistent setting immediately; consider a switch or checkbox.
An icon alone would make the action ambiguous.

variants.default: One primary action in the current surface or a high-confidence confirmation.
variants.secondary: A supporting action that still needs a filled surface next to the primary action.
variants.outline: Secondary actions with a visible boundary, including toolbar actions such as Refresh.
variants.ghost: Tertiary, reversible, or low-emphasis actions and dense toolbars.
variants.destructive: Actions that delete or discard data; pair with an explicit confirmation step.
variants.link: Inline actions that read as part of surrounding text.

sizes.default: Standard control height for pages and dialogs.
sizes.sm: Dense surfaces such as table rows and card toolbars.
sizes.xs: The most compact chrome, such as inline tag actions.
sizes.icon: Icon-only actions; requires an aria-label and has icon-xs, icon-sm, and icon-lg counterparts.

button.iconSlots: Mark leading icons with data-icon="inline-start" and trailing icons with data-icon="inline-end" so the button balances its padding.
accessibility: Use an action-first visible label; icon-only buttons need an aria-label.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate destructive or status meaning.
Keep the accessible name and width stable during processing.
Use native disabled semantics when the action cannot run.

admin-page.purpose: Provide standard content width, responsive gutters, and bottom spacing for Kiwi Admin pages.

admin-page-header.purpose: Provide a semantic page heading, optional description, status, back action, and responsive actions.

navigation-sidebar.purpose: Collapsible admin navigation rail on the shared semantic tokens, with fixed icon geometry, tooltip labels when collapsed, and animated nested navigation.

admin-form.purpose: Provide Admin-specific composition helpers that implement the general Forms guidance.
admin-form.note: AdminFormSurface, AdminFormSection, and AdminFormActions are still MUI implementations pending shadcn migration; the Storybook form examples compose the same structure from shadcn primitives.

forms.purpose: Define a shared design and interaction contract for forms across Kiwi without prescribing one page-specific component.
forms.definition: A form is a structured task that helps users provide, review, validate, and submit related information with a clear outcome.
principles: Ask only for information required to complete the current task; defer advanced or conditional fields until they become relevant.
Create hierarchy with labels, section headings, spacing, and dividers before adding containers or elevation.
Keep the path from the first field to the primary action predictable, with one clear completion action per form.
Preserve entered data through validation errors and explain how each problem can be corrected.
anatomy: Heading: names the task and briefly explains its outcome when context is not already obvious.
Sections: group fields by user goal or concept, not by backend model or API shape.
Fields: use persistent visible labels, appropriate input types, and concise supporting text only when needed.
Feedback: place validation and recovery guidance beside the related field, with a summary when several errors block submission.
Actions: present one primary completion action and visually subordinate cancel, back, or secondary actions.
layout: Use a single vertical field column by default; place fields side by side only when their relationship is obvious and both remain readable at narrower widths.
Keep a consistent 16–24px rhythm between related fields and 32–48px between major sections.
Prefer whitespace or dividers between sections. Use an outlined zero-elevation surface only when the form needs a boundary from adjacent content.
Keep long-form controls within a readable content width instead of stretching inputs across the full page.
Stack fields and actions before labels, values, or controls become compressed; avoid horizontal page scrolling.
fields: Use visible labels rather than placeholder-only instructions.
Mark required and optional expectations consistently, and avoid asking users to infer them from validation failures.
Choose semantic input types and browser autocomplete values where available.
Use helper text for format or consequence, not to repeat the label.
Use disabled for unavailable controls and read-only for inspectable values that cannot be edited.
validation: Validate after a field loses focus or when the user submits; do not show an error before the user has had a reasonable chance to complete the field.
State what is wrong and how to fix it beside the related field. Do not rely on color alone.
On failed submission, preserve all entered values, focus the first invalid field, and provide an error summary when multiple fields are affected.
For server errors, distinguish field-specific problems from form-level failures and provide a retry or recovery path.
actions: Use one contained primary action for the form outcome. Use outlined or text treatment for secondary actions.
Use action-first labels such as Save changes or Create class instead of generic labels such as Submit.
During submission, prevent duplicate requests, keep the button label and width stable, and show progress without clearing the form.
Confirm success near the form or destination; do not leave users guessing whether their changes were saved.
For long forms, actions may remain visible while scrolling if they do not cover content or detach from the form context.
accessibility: Associate every control with a visible label and connect helper or error text through the control's accessible description.
Keep keyboard focus order aligned with the visual sequence and preserve a visible focus indicator.
Group related choices with fieldset and legend semantics when appropriate.
Keep interactive controls at least 44px high and ensure text and state indicators meet contrast requirements.
Announce asynchronous errors and success feedback without unexpectedly moving focus.

examples.role: Default, error, and disabled state example

small-popup.purpose: Define a shared visual and interaction contract for small anchored overlays without prescribing one content-specific component.
small-popup.definition: A transient surface anchored to a trigger for a short local choice, action set, or compact bounded task.
useWhen: A trigger opens a short menu, selector, or bounded local task next to its point of origin.
The content can be understood and completed without the stronger interruption of a dialog.
avoidWhen: The flow needs a page-level decision, destructive confirmation, or long multi-section form; use a dialog or dedicated page.
The content is only a short explanation with no interaction; use a tooltip.
The content needs persistent comparison with the page; use an inline panel or dedicated surface.
anatomy: Trigger: names the choice or action and exposes expanded state when applicable.
Surface: the anchored floating container with bounded width, elevation, and viewport collision handling.
Header (optional): a short title or search field only when the content needs orientation or filtering.
Content: a concise action list, selector, or compact picker using one primary type role.
Footer (optional): only for bounded tasks that need explicit Apply or Cancel actions.

contentPatterns.use: A short list of immediate commands or mutually exclusive choices.
A variable option set that needs filtering before selection.
A bounded local task, such as selecting a date range, that may need an explicit apply action.

typography.fontFamily: Inherit Montserrat from the Kiwi theme; do not introduce a popup-local font family.

roles.label: Popup title
roles.use: Optional short section or picker title. Do not use it for every simple menu.

roles.label: Primary popup text
roles.use: Trigger labels, menu options, field values, calendar dates, compact actions, and preset choices.

roles.label: Supporting text
roles.use: Field labels, keyboard hints, weekday labels, metadata, and brief helper text. This is the minimum text size in a small popup.

rules: Keep external trigger text and corresponding internal text on the same role so opening the popup does not create an unexpected type-scale jump.
Use 0.875rem for popup titles and all primary popup text; do not introduce a 13px intermediate size.
Use only the title, primary, and supporting roles; do not introduce ad-hoc intermediate sizes.
Never render popup text below 0.75rem. Small type is for short labels and metadata, not paragraphs or long-form reading.
Use text.primary for choices and values, text.secondary for supporting content, and preserve at least WCAG 4.5:1 contrast for normal text.
Use Fade for both entrance and exit.
Do not add scale, translate, blur, spring, or stagger to small popup surfaces.
Keep opening and closing geometry stable; motion must not shift the trigger or surrounding layout.

layout: Keep the popup anchored to its trigger and inside the viewport with a 12px minimum viewport margin.
Choose the narrowest width that keeps common labels and controls readable; short menus can start at 184px and searchable selectors can extend to 360px.
Use compact 8–16px internal spacing and bounded scrolling for variable option lists.
Keep pointer targets at least 40px high on compact desktop surfaces and 44px high on touch-oriented surfaces.
Reserve elevation and shadow for the floating surface; static filter bars and trigger groups remain flat or outlined.
interaction: Open from an explicit trigger and close after a completed immediate choice.
Close on outside click and Escape; keep draft state until Apply for bounded picker tasks.
Return focus to the trigger after close and preserve visible focus while navigating inside.
Do not show a visual Escape badge; keyboard dismissal remains supported without adding persistent UI noise.
accessibility: Use the matching menu or popover semantics (shadcn DropdownMenu/Select on Base UI; MUI Menu/Popover only on legacy surfaces), preserve keyboard navigation and Escape dismissal, and return focus to the trigger on close.
Give icon-only triggers an accessible name and expose expanded and controlled state where applicable.
Do not use color alone for selected, disabled, error, or status meaning.

examples.role: Compact picker product reference (MUI implementation pending shadcn migration)

metricContracts.definition: Distinct entity identifiers across the full selected range.
metricContracts.presentation: Use for a headline total that answers how many distinct entities were in scope.

metricContracts.definition: Distinct entity identifiers within each calendar day. One entity may appear in multiple daily points.
metricContracts.presentation: Use for trend shape. Do not sum daily points and present the result as a range-unique total.

metricContracts.definition: Every event is assigned to exactly one exhaustive category.
metricContracts.presentation: Breakdown categories must be mutually exclusive when their sum is expected to match a headline total.

metricContracts.definition: Entities ranked by a primary aggregate, with a secondary count used as supporting context.
metricContracts.presentation: State whether the source is range-filtered. Do not imply a filter that the API does not implement.

do: Define aggregation, deduplication key, time zone, and range before naming a metric.
Use one term consistently in card title, tooltip, and empty state.
Make chart categories exhaustive and mutually exclusive when totals must reconcile.
avoid: Use two labels for the same metric at different levels of the page.
Compare a range-unique total with the sum of daily unique values.
Count one event in both a parent category and one of its subcategories.

do: Let CardContent own visual padding and keep Recharts margin at zero by default.
Add a small 8px chart margin only where dots or strokes need clipping protection.
Set explicit axis width, axis height, and tickMargin; Recharts defaults consume hidden space.
Use a compact fixed height for time-series cards; longer ranges add horizontal points, not useful height.
Use horizontal bars when category labels are longer than the available card width.
avoid: Stack Card padding, chart container padding, and Recharts margin.
Increase chart height based only on date-range length.
Rotate long X-axis labels when a horizontal bar chart communicates the same data more clearly.
Remove every pixel of safety space when visible dots or active dots touch the SVG boundary.

reviewChecklist: Do headline totals and detail charts reconcile under the documented aggregation?
Are section titles categories and card titles exact visualizations?
Are all card subtitles fixed descriptive copy?
Does changing the date immediately show Skeleton without flashing old data?
Can a stale request overwrite data or stop a newer loading state?
Does Refresh include every persistent page API and preserve button dimensions?
Are loading, empty, error, and loaded layouts the same size?
Are Recharts axes and margins explicitly sized?
Do desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts use the available width intentionally?
Do long labels, identifiers, units, tooltips, headings, and dialog controls remain accessible?

delivery.purpose: Define required evidence for accessible, responsive, visually stable, density-aware, and network-resilient Kiwi interfaces.

documentationLayers.ai: Concise contract lists stored in qualityGuides.delivery.contracts of this catalog, rendered into the Quality guide and marked with data-ai-contract.
documentationLayers.human: Responsive visual examples for viewport composition, skeleton geometry, network recovery, information density, and field growth.
documentationLayers.executable: Product-specific stories, interaction tests, accessibility checks, and composed surface reviews.

accessibility: Navigate every interactive element with the keyboard in a logical order and keep a visible focus indicator.
Use descriptive accessible names, semantic heading order, native disabled behavior, and sufficient contrast.
Do not communicate status with color alone. Announce loading and actionable errors with appropriate live semantics.
Keep recovery actions reachable without a pointer and run the Storybook Accessibility panel on every materially changed state.
viewport: Test the actual viewport at 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440 px unless the product contract defines a more relevant matrix.
Verify component stories and composed surfaces; inner-wrapper resizing alone is insufficient.
Fail the review for unintended page-level horizontal scrolling, covered actions, unreachable dialogs, or content that loses hierarchy.
network: Model initial loading, background refresh, settled, successful empty, offline, timeout, server error, and recovery as distinct states.
Make the skeleton approximate the final hierarchy and dimensions so loading does not create layout shift.
Preserve useful content and user input during refresh or failure, prevent duplicate actions, and expose an accessible recovery path.
density: Plan density around the user task: keep status, decision-critical fields, and primary actions visible in the common working viewport.
Reject layouts that create large decorative gaps, and reject layouts that compress labels, targets, or hierarchy until they become hard to scan or operate.
Use a deliberate spacing and type scale; do not solve density by applying one global compact or spacious value.
fieldGrowth: Define the expected field-count range, longest label, longest value, optional-field behavior, and the threshold that changes the layout.
Keep titles, summaries, and primary actions anchored when optional fields appear or disappear.
When a variable secondary region exceeds its planned height, contain it with an accessible labelled scroll area or switch to a dedicated detail view.
Avoid nested scrolling, hidden focused content, and scroll containers that separate users from the primary action or critical error.

viewportChecks.label: minimum narrow surface
viewportChecks.purpose: Detect clipped controls, unreadable wrapping, broken touch targets, and accidental horizontal scrolling.

viewportChecks.label: representative phone
viewportChecks.purpose: Verify the intended mobile composition, action stacking, navigation, dialogs, and keyboard-safe form layout.

viewportChecks.label: tablet
viewportChecks.purpose: Verify transitions between stacked and multi-column layouts and ensure neither mobile nor desktop assumptions leave unused or overlapping space.

viewportChecks.label: compact desktop
viewportChecks.purpose: Check the layout with navigation, side panels, and tables competing for width.

viewportChecks.label: wide desktop
viewportChecks.purpose: Enforce readable line length and intentional maximum widths; content should not become sparse or stretched simply because space is available.

networkChecks.evidence: Settled baseline, no unnecessary flicker, and no duplicate submission.
Visible loading feedback with reserved final dimensions.
Existing content remains available and is marked as refreshing or stale.
Dedicated actionable error state rather than a successful empty state.
Input preservation, duplicate prevention, and a recoverable retry path.
Retry reaches the valid settled state without duplicated data or actions.

densityChecks.evidence: Small data sets retain grouping and hierarchy without decorative empty expansion.
Decision-critical fields and the primary action fit the representative working viewport.
Labels, values, targets, and hierarchy remain readable without page-level horizontal overflow.
The documented wrap, stack, bounded-scroll, or dedicated-detail fallback activates predictably.
Optional fields disappear without leaving broken gaps or moving primary anchors unpredictably.
Variable secondary content is contained at a documented threshold while primary actions remain outside the scroll region.
